extracted.intended_audience: airlines and other aircraft operators; aircraft passengers traveling to the United States from the People's Republic of China; U.S. public health and enforcement officials
extracted.subtask_description: A CDC Notice and Order specifying who is covered and the exact documentary, attestation, verification, and exception requirements for negative pre-departure SARS-CoV-2 tests or documentation of recovery for air passengers traveling to the United States from the People's Republic of China (including implementation obligations for airlines/aircraft operators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / Covered Passengers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits the boarding of passengers 2 years of age or older on an itinerary that includes the United States on: any aircraft departing from the People's Republic of China, or any aircraft departing from a Designated Airport if the passenger has been in the People's Republic of China within the ten (10) days prior to their departure for the United States, unless the passenger presents paper or digital documentation of a Qualifying Test or Documentation of Recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies regardless of citizenship or vaccination status. Excludes passengers transiting the People's Republic of China for a period of 24 hours or less en route to the United States, and excludes passengers who have been in the People's Republic of China for less than 24 hours. Children under age 2 are not subject to the requirement; a parent/authorized individual may present documentation for passengers aged 2–17. The Order covers any flight that includes the United States as final or intermediate stop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying Test timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Qualifying Test is a SARS-CoV-2 viral test conducted on a specimen collected no more than 2 calendar days before the passenger's departure from the People's Republic of China or a Designated Airport (if the passenger has been in the PRC within the prior 10 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specimen collection date must be shown on the test result to verify the ≤2-calendar-day window before the flight's departure. CDC may later adjust timing via guidance or enforcement discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying Test result content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of a negative SARS-CoV-2 viral test result must include: (i) personal identifiers (e.g., name and date of birth) that match the passenger's passport or travel documents; (ii) a specimen collection date indicating collection no more than 2 calendar days before the flight's departure; (iii) the type of viral test indicating it is a NAAT or antigen test; (iv) a test result that states “NEGATIVE,” “SARS-CoV-2 RNA NOT DETECTED,” “SARS-CoV-2 ANTIGEN NOT DETECTED,” or “COVID-19 NOT DETECTED,” or other indication that SARS-CoV-2 was not detected (a test marked “invalid” is not acceptable); and (v) information about the entity issuing the result (e.g., laboratory, healthcare entity, or telehealth service), such as name and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Airlines must confirm all these elements before boarding. The personal identifiers must match passport/travel documents to avoid identity-swapping. Tests marked invalid are explicitly unacceptable. The Order contemplates both paper and digital test results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and authorization of Viral Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Viral Test means a viral detection test for current infection with SARS-CoV-2, i.e., a nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) or a viral antigen test. The test must be cleared, approved, or issued an emergency use authorization by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or granted marketing authorization by the relevant national authority, for the detection of SARS-CoV-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only NAAT or antigen tests with appropriate regulatory authorization are acceptable as Qualifying Tests; airlines should verify that the issuing entity performed an authorized viral detection test. CDC may exercise enforcement discretion to align with evolving guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of Recovery — positive test >10 and <91 days before flight
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of Recovery may be a positive SARS-CoV-2 viral test result from a specimen collected more than 10 calendar days but fewer than 91 calendar days before the flight's departure. The positive test result must include: (i) personal identifiers matching travel documents; (ii) a specimen collection date in the required window; (iii) information that the test performed was a viral test (NAAT or antigen); (iv) a test result indicating detection (e.g., “POSITIVE,” “SARS-CoV-2 RNA DETECTED,” etc.; invalid is not acceptable); and (v) information about the issuing entity (name and contact information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This path permits recovered passengers to travel without a negative test if their positive viral test falls into the 11–90 day window; airlines must verify the same identifier and issuer elements as for negative tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of Recovery — positive test ≤10 days before flight PLUS healthcare/provider letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatively, Documentation of Recovery may be a positive SARS-CoV-2 viral test result from a specimen collected 10 or fewer calendar days before the flight's departure AND a signed letter from a licensed healthcare provider or public health official stating that the passenger's COVID-19 symptoms began more than 10 full calendar days before the flight's departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter must list the date the passenger's symptoms started; include personal identifiers (name and DOB) that match passport/travel documents; be signed and dated on official letterhead containing the name, address, and phone number of the healthcare provider or public health official. The associated positive test must still include the test-type, specimen collection date, positive detection wording, issuer contact info, and matching personal identifiers. Airlines must verify both the test and the letter before boarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passenger attestation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Passengers (or their authorized representative) 2 years of age or older must complete and provide the attached attestation (Attachment A) stating they have received a negative Qualifying Test, meet the criteria for Documentation of Recovery, or have a Humanitarian Exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation may be completed in paper or digital form. The attestation is a statement under 18 U.S.C. 1001 (false statements can carry criminal penalties). One attestation form must be filled out for each passenger age 2 or older. A parent or authorized individual may complete the attestation for passengers aged 2–17 or for those unable to act on their own behalf. Airlines are encouraged to incorporate the attestation into paperless check-in; third parties may collect attestations but the airline remains legally responsible for accuracy and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airline / aircraft operator verification and boarding prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any airline or other aircraft operator boarding passengers subject to the Order must: identify which passengers are subject; confirm that each such passenger, prior to boarding, has presented paper or digital documentation reflecting a Qualifying Test or Documentation of Recovery or meets a specified exception; verify each passenger has attested to one of the listed options; and not board any passenger without confirming the documentation and attestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Airlines must retain a copy of each passenger attestation for 2 years. Failure to comply may subject the airline/operator to criminal penalties under cited statutes. Airlines cannot shift legal responsibility to third parties that collect attestations or translations; the airline remains responsible for accuracy and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and production of documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each passenger must retain paper or digital documentation presented to the airline reflecting either (a) a negative result for the Qualifying Test or (b) Documentation of Recovery. Upon request, the passenger (or authorized representative) must produce such documentation to any U.S. Government official or a cooperating state or local public health authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passengers should keep copies of test results and any recovery letters after arrival as they may be requested. Airlines must retain attestations for 2 years and be prepared to produce to authorities if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order excepts: (a) crew members on official duty assigned by the airline/operator involving operation/positioning of crew when covered under an occupational health and safety program consistent with CDC guidance; (b) airlines/operators transporting passengers with COVID-19 on certain authorized non-scheduled flights with infection control measures; (c) U.S. Federal law enforcement personnel on official orders carrying out law enforcement functions when covered under appropriate occupational health measures (but not when traveling for training/business); (d) U.S. military personnel and associated persons when traveling on U.S. military assets under competent orders and force health protection guidance; and (e) individuals for whom a humanitarian exception is necessary based on exigent circumstances and inability to access/complete pre-departure testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exception has conditions (e.g., occupational health programs, CDC authorization for special flights). Humanitarian exceptions require documentation; see separate Humanitarian Exception rubric. Airlines/operators should verify exception eligibility before boarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanitarian Exception (documentation and attestation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Humanitarian Exception may be granted in exigent circumstances where emergency travel is required to preserve health and safety and pre-departure testing cannot be accessed or completed before travel. The attestation includes an option (C) for a Humanitarian Exception documented by a letter from the U.S. Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passengers claiming a humanitarian exception must have a U.S. Government letter documenting the exception. Airlines must accept and record the attestation option and retain it per retention rules. The Order indicates humanitarian exceptions are narrowly drawn (e.g., emergency medical evacuations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Airports and CDC discretion to add airports
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Airports are airports outside of the People's Republic of China where the requirements apply if the passenger has been in the People's Republic of China within the prior ten (10) days; designated examples include Incheon International Airport (ICN), Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ), and Vancouver International Airport (YVR). CDC may list additional Designated Airports in guidance associated with the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDC will consider travel patterns and emergence of variants when adding airports. Airlines should consult CDC guidance and the Order for the current list of Designated Airports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled free pratique and carrier conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 42 CFR 71.31(b), this Notice and Order constitutes a controlled free pratique to any airline or other aircraft operator boarding passengers subject to the requirements of the Order at an airport in the People's Republic of China or a Designated Airport; under this controlled free pratique, the airline/operator must comply with the conditions outlined in the Order to receive permission for the aircraft to enter and disembark passengers within the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carriers must view compliance as a condition of entry/disembarkation permission. Noncompliance could lead to denial of praticque or other administrative actions in addition to criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement, penalties, and false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order states any airline/operator or passenger who fails to comply may be subject to criminal penalties under, inter alia, 42 U.S.C. 271 and 42 CFR 71.2, in conjunction with 18 U.S.C. 3559 and 3571. Willfully giving false or misleading information may result in criminal penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001. The Order is enforceable through cited statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passengers and airlines should understand that false attestations or failure to comply can result in denial of boarding, delays, future boarding denial, criminal fines, and imprisonment. The CDC may exercise enforcement discretion to adjust scope/requirements and will announce such changes on CDC's website and via amended Federal Register publications as practicable.
